entries.title: Global behavior roster + enablement lens — mirror the shortlist that gates swarm sharing
entries.note: One switch, one meaning: the Beehaviors window grew a ROSTER mode (header tune button; opened by the mesh toggle's WORLD stage and the join selector's 'choose shared beehaviors') listing every behavior with a global on/off switch. Off = dormant everywhere — icons, view toggles and offers vanish; decorations stay on their tiles — AND withheld from every swarm (wire kind 30208 on the lifecycle channel; adopters record hc:withheld-at-roots at the fold, the snapshot layer arrives untouched). Per-tile wake exceptions (hc:behavior-wake, subtree-covering) outrank the global off; re-enabling globally wakes everything, exceptions and hidden records untouched. Precedence: wake ON > global OFF > per-tile hidden > ON. Owed under behaviors/swarm + the behaviors deck: a card for the roster mode, part tiles for sharing/behavior-enablement.ts (essentials reader), features-viewer/behavior-enablement.ts (shell writer), the dormancy gates (visual-bee-icons, view.bee, tile-view creation row, show-features stamps), swarm.drone 30208 publish/receive and the swarm-adopt fold recorder — pheromone-marked, notes carrying the one-switch doctrine. note-add is additive; keep out of the idle drain.

entries.title: The bakery walkthrough — one tile becomes a world, verb by verb
entries.note: scripts/presentation/walkthrough.cjs renders the worked-example reel walkthrough/hypercomb-walkthrough.mp4: one concept (a neighborhood bakery) grown from a single tile into a three-level plan by /atomize (parts fan out), travel-inside, /expand twice (the shelf gains only the siblings it was missing, then gets crowded), /organize (the session answers with a plan, the hive moves the tiles), a stacked /atomize on sourdough, and a full-tree map. Every verb beat shows the honest machinery: the command line, the ask minted as a honey hex flying to the parked-claude-session badge, and honey-glow marking only what the verb just made. Twenty-six flat-vector art glyphs (no text in the art) in the shell's honey palette. Narrated by the same neural voice and audio cache as the last rendered full presentation. Owed under the presentation mirror: a 'walkthrough' chapter tile beside the verbs chapter holding one part tile per beat (open, seed, ask-atomize, atomize, travel, expand, crowded, organize, deep-atomize, map, close) with its say line as the note, pheromone-marked as part of the presentation production; the behaviors-deck cards for /atomize, /organize and /expand gain a note pointing at this cut as the worked example with the bridge machinery visible. note-add is additive — keep out of the idle drain.

entries.title: Note the closure guards on behaviors/structure/reference
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive, re-running lands the note twice. Two guards landed in sharing/decoration-closure.ts: (1) reference records get a kind-scoped closure fallback — a record minted past buildReferenceRecord (hand-rolled writer, bridge script) still carries payload.requiredBouquet on push AND adopt, so a shared portal's demand is always expandable on arrival; (2) collectSigsDeep now skips targetSig keys beside groupSig — targetSig is an identity pointer in every use (a reference's lineage address, a feedback item being retired), so writeDecoration's refs auto-declare can never mint a permanent 404 cascade from it. Doctrine line for the note: the closure carries DEPENDENCIES, never REFERENTS. Add as a note on the behaviors/structure/reference tile, beside the existing /requires bouquet note.
